notes: 2Modern.com is a Shopify store using Searchspring (siteId dja4ih) as its search/facet layer; server HTML always shows a placeholder, so qty was read from the Searchspring search.json API with bgfilter.collection_handle=<handle>, the same layer the live page itself renders from (confirmed by og:title match). Every qty below was pagination-exhaustion-checked (resultsPerPage=100, first page count + last page begin/end arithmetic reconciling exactly to totalResults). Checked: desktop mega-menu, mobile nav dropdown (secondary 'New'-menu block plus each department's own mega-menu column), footer, sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1/2.xml (2879 collection URLs grepped for best/top/popular/trending/customer-favorite terms), and internal site search (q=best-sellers not tried since nav already gave canonical link). FOUND: (1) /collections/best-sellers - standalone top-nav item 'Best Sellers' (data-handle=best-sellers), page <title> 'Top Selling & Most Viewed Modern Design at 2Modern', og:title 'Best Sellers'; no further children nested under this exact nav item. (2) Six department-level 'Best Selling <Dept>' collections that are each linked as a column-header link inside that department's OWN mega-menu (Furniture, Lighting, Outdoor, Rugs, Decor, Tabletop) rather than under the Best Sellers nav item itself - treated as genuine site-exposed children of the same Bestsellers concept per brief Sec.3 and grouped under the Best Sellers parent row. Each of these six is a flat leaf in its own menu column (no further sub-items nested under them, confirmed by reading surrounding HTML - e.g. 'Best Selling Lighting' sits alone next to 'Lighting on Sale' with nothing else in that column). (3) /collections/trending-now - linked in the secondary navbar's 'New' mega-menu as its own heading ('Trending Now'), page <title> 'Trending Now', a genuine real product listing (verified real product titles in the API response), matches the brief's 'Trending Products' target term; kept as a sibling Bestsellers-concept row, NOT merged with best-sellers (different qty, different product mix - mugs/glassware/candle holders vs. the furniture/lighting-heavy best-sellers list). EXCLUDED as non-qualifying: sibling links under the same 'Trending Now' menu column that are themed style/trend campaigns, not popularity listings - '2026 Trend Report' (blog), 'Scanditalia', 'Into The Woods', 'New Romantics', 'Art-Driven Interiors', 'Neo Deco'. EXCLUDED brand-specific bestseller rollups found only via sitemap grep, never linked in any nav menu I found (per brief's brand-rollup exclusion convention used on this company's earlier Home-Decor pass): pablo-best-sellers, troy-lighting-best-sellers, flos-best-sellers, tom-dixon-best-sellers, hinkley-best-sellers, gus-best-sellers, modern-forms-best-sellers. EXCLUDED B2B-audience rollups (not a product-category cut, a different customer segment): best-selling-trade-designs, best-selling-trade-lighting, best-selling-trade-furniture, best-selling-trade-decor, best-selling-trade-outdoor. EXCLUDED narrower facet re-cuts that exist as live Shopify collections per the sitemap but are not linked from ANY nav menu (grepped the full best-sellers.html page source and found none of these as links) - treated as orphan facet pages rather than genuine site-exposed sub-structure, same treatment the prior Home-Decor pass gave to this site's Rugs-by-Shape/Size re-cuts: best-selling-dining-tables, best-selling-beds, best-selling-ceiling-fans, best-selling-pendants, best-selling-chandeliers, best-selling-wall-lights, best-selling-seating, best-selling-tables, best-selling-bedroom-furniture, best-selling-planters, best-selling-tabletop-decor (this last one IS also the exact handle used for the linked 'Best Selling Tabletop' row, so it was kept once as that row, not double-counted), best-selling-wallpaper, best-selling-outdoor-designs (also already kept once as the linked 'Best Selling Outdoor' row). No robots.txt Claude-disallow; no WAF encountered; all access via tier-1 direct HTTP fetch + Searchspring API, no Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome needed.
